c1696760fc378cd5: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded those calling for the party to leave the unity government that Umno played an important role in its formation.
He said any attempt to remove the party from the government should instead be done formally through a vote in the Dewan Rakyat.
"Ceplos... do not challenge Umno to leave the unity government," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
"The unity government was formed because of Umno, you know. The Prime Minister became Prime Minister because of Umno's support," he added.
4e1b2fd1cec0f154: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must translate its Malaysia Blue Agenda into sustained grassroots efforts to strengthen public confidence ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16), said party vice-president Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail.
He said the agenda, introduced by party president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, would not move forward on its own and required the involvement of all party members.
"The agenda must be translated into action and brought to the grassroots so that the Blue Wave phenomenon that has begun can become a Blue Tsunami across the country.

"We need to build relationships with the people, not only during elections, but all the time," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
Wan Rosdy said the party also needed to strengthen public trust through tangible service and give people reasons to continue having confidence in Umno.
"Efforts to win the people's hearts must be carried out through work that can be seen, language that resonates with the people and leadership that understands their concerns.
"The people do not want to hear what we say. They want to see what we do for them.
"The Malaysia Blue Agenda should not be seen merely as a colour or slogan. Instead, it must be measured by the party's ability to turn public support and presence into votes and victory," he said.
He said the movement must begin as an idea, develop into a movement, build public confidence and eventually translate into votes and victory at GE16.
449ecf4a1533e245: KUALA LUMPUR: Badminton Asia (BA) has confirmed that the so-called Asian Games men's team draw circulating on social media is fake.

The fake draw has raised concerns among Malaysian fans as Malaysia were drawn to meet a dangerous Hong Kong in the last-16 of the men's event and were set to face top seeds China in a possible quarter-final clash.
BA secretary-general Datuk Kenny Goh said the actual team draw will be conducted during the team managers' meeting on Sept 19, with the competition beginning on Sept 20.

"There are two events — individual and team events. For the team events, the draw will be conducted during the team managers' meeting on Sept 19. This is already in the Asian Games handbook," said Kenny on Saturday.
"If you check, the rankings (seedings) of the teams have been published yesterday.
"After the conclusion of the team events (Oct 24), they will conduct the individual draw on the same day.
"We can't do anything about it (fake draw) and have to ignore it because even the seedings were wrong."
Based on the seedings, Malaysia are seeded sixth, while the top four seeds are Indonesia, China, Taiwan and Japan. India and South Korea are seeded fifth and seventh respectively.
This means Malaysia could face one of the top four seeds, who will receive a first-round bye, in the quarter-finals.
In the women's team event, China, Japan, South Korea and Japan are the top four seeds, while Malaysia are seeded seventh behind Thailand and Indonesia.
b0881f3650eb5880: KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 12 — The Public Service Commission (SPA) has filled more than 1,000 nursing vacancies in the public service to date, with open interviews being conducted to expedite the recruitment process.

Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the move was among its immediate efforts to address the need to fill critical posts, particularly nurses, who are in high demand in the healthcare sector.
“To date, we need more than 1,400 (nurses) and we have already filled more than 1,000. So, we still need several hundred more to be filled urgently.

“These efforts are ongoing from time to time because there are also nursing positions that require candidates to undergo training, and this training takes time,” he told reporters after officiating at the SPA Madani Adopted Village Project Handover Ceremony at Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein here today.
Also present were Department of Orang Asli Development Director-General Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad, SPA Secretary Datuk Ikhbal Hanam Mukras and Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein village head Din Alang.

Ahmad Jailani said the open interview and walk-in methods were introduced early this year through several career carnivals organised by SPA nationwide, providing more opportunities for qualified youths to join the public service.

He said candidates with a diploma in nursing could walk in for an interview, while those who had yet to submit an online application could also complete their SPA application at the interview centre before attending the session.

“This is also a breakthrough effort that we have undertaken to expedite the process. If we use the usual process, there may sometimes be delays. Apart from nurses, SPA is also focusing on filling several other critical positions that require urgent recruitment, including Public Health Assistants.

“The demand for nurses is quite high, particularly as the healthcare industry has become increasingly important in the country. Therefore, the target is usually (recruiting) nurses into the public service, as the possibly better offers in the private sector mean that a large proportion of them join (the private sector) rather than the public service,” he said.

Meanwhile, Ahmad Jailani, who is also chairman of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission, said the government did not prevent civil servants from seeking better employment opportunities after completing their contracts but instead, SPA would ensure that succession plans were implemented by continuously recruiting new personnel.

“They have contracts that have been stipulated in their appointments. However, once their contracts expire, they are free. We cannot prevent any government officers from seeking better employment opportunities.

“So, there are no restrictions in this regard and we give them the freedom to do so. Nevertheless, we believe the important thing is the succession plan, and we will find ways to recruit new personnel. I am confident that if we go to places such as Felda Chenein in Lenggong, we can find youths who want to join the service,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: The initials SPA stand for Suruhanjaya Perkhidmatan Awam, the Public Service Commission’s name in Malay.

7ce14639ac13b1a1: GEORGE TOWN: Police have clarified that a fatal accident involving an 81-year-old pedestrian at Desa Green was not a hit-and-run.
The victim, a retiree, died at the scene after she reportedly tripped and fell onto the road in front of a moving Proton Saga in the flat's parking area at 2.20pm on Sept 8.

Northeast district Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Deputy Superintendent Donny John Jubang said initial reports had suggested a hit-and-run, but closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage proved otherwise.
"Based on the CCTV recording obtained, the driver stopped on the left shoulder immediately after the accident and got out to assist the victim," Donny said when contacted today.
"There was no element of a hit-and-run, contrary to the initial information received."
The victim suffered severe head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Donny added that the driver, a 60-year-old retiree, was uninjured.

"The driver was subsequently traced and lodged a police report at 10.38pm the same day," Donny said. "The driver has been released on bail, taking into consideration his health condition, including heart disease and hypertension, and his need to make frequent visits to Penang Hospital for treatment."

46c725d9926564de: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has warned against challenging the party to leave the unity government.
The deputy prime minister said any move to remove Umno should instead be followed by a fresh mandate from voters or a no-confidence vote in the Dewan Rakyat.
"Although the current number of seats gives a comfortable majority, that is because additional parties have joined, bringing the total to 18.
"If we are asked to leave, logically, if the original 112 is no longer there, a new mandate should be obtained.

"There are two options. First, obtain a fresh mandate by holding a general election. Second, remove us formally and hold a no-confidence vote in the Dewan Rakyat," he said while winding up the debate on his policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
"If they are brave enough, call it (the next general election) now," he said to shouts from delegates who chants inunison the word "bubar" (dissolve).
c028cc0ea016b1b5: KUALA LUMPUR: Naib Presiden Umno, Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail berkata kerjasama antara Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Pakatan Harapan (PH) antara pilihan paling 'selesa' untuk mengekalkan kemenangan BN di Pahang pada PRU16.
Menteri besar Pahang itu berkata, dapatan itu diperoleh menerusi kajian perintis yang dijalankan bersama kepimpinan Umno Bahagian di negeri berkenaan bagi menilai tiga senario jajaran politik.
Katanya, tiga senario itu adalah kerjasama BN dengan PH, kerjasama BN dengan Perikatan Nasional (PN) dan akhir sekali BN bertanding solo.
"Yang menariknya, daripada tiga kajian tersebut, semuanya BN boleh menang.
“Rumusannya, nak selesa, nak cuci tangan, dengan PH. Kalau dengan PN hilang 15% pengundi Cina, tetapi masih boleh menang.
"Kalau solo, masih boleh menang tetapi risikonya sangat tinggi," katanya ketika menyampaikan ucapan penggulungan di Perhimpunan Agung Umno di Pusat Dagangan Dunia hari ini.
Bagaimanapun, Wan Rosdy berkata, keputusan muktamad berhubung bentuk kerjasama politik di Pahang masih dalam perbincangan dan bakal ditentukan pucuk pimpinan parti.

"Setakat hari ini masih lagi dalam perbincangan. Insya-Allah apabila semua maklumat dapat diperolehi, saya dan rakan-rakan akan mengadap presiden untuk berbincang lebih lanjut sebelum membuat keputusan," katanya.
Dalam pada itu, Wan Rosdy berkata Pahang merupakan satu-satunya negeri yang mengekalkan pentadbiran BN tanpa putus.
Malah beliau berikrar untuk mempertahankan kubu kuat parti itu daripada jatuh ke tangan pihak lain.
“Hanya Pahang sahaja yang DNA-nya tidak putus Umno yang memerintah negeri ini. Negeri lain pernah terputus, tetapi Pahang tidak pernah,” katanya.
Pada PRU15 menyaksikan BN dan PN masing-masing memperoleh 17 kerusi DUN, manakala PH mendapat lapan kerusi. BN membentuk kerajaan negeri selepas mendapat sokongan Adun PH.
e06ecd775dba9c80: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — The Blue Malaysia Agenda outlined by Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi will be reflected in Barisan Nasional’s (BN) manifesto for the 16th General Election (GE16), says BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the agenda formed part of the coalition’s efforts to formulate an approach that ensured Malaysia remained peaceful and stable, while navigating current and future challenges.

“The president outlined eight initiatives under the Blue Malaysia Agenda… all of which are crucial to ensuring the nation stays peaceful and stable, while demonstrating our resolve to address current challenges.

“For instance, amid an increasingly volatile global landscape, careful planning is required to ensure Malaysia remains peaceful and prosperous,” he told reporters at the Media Centre during the Umno General Assembly 2026 at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur today.

Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid said Umno and BN would outline the Blue Malaysia Agenda to shape the nation’s trajectory heading towards the centenary of its independence, should the coalition return to lead Putrajaya.
The agenda carries aspirations to build a sovereign and united Malaysia, an innovative and high-income nation, a prosperous and equitable society, and a globally respected country. — Bernama
abc86badfc0edb6f: KUALA LUMPUR: Perpecahan Melayu akan mengurangkan rasa hormat dan rasa yakin dalam kalangan parti politik di Sarawak dan Sabah terhadap parti Melayu di Semenanjung untuk mengemudi pemerintahan Malaysia, dakwa Naib Presiden Umno, Khaled Nordin.
Beliau berkata kuasa politik Melayu yang 'bercempera', 'berantakan' dan 'berpecah' mempamerkan kelemahan parti Melayu di Semenanjung sebagai pemerintah yang berwibawa dan berprestasi.

"Jika kita tidak boleh mengurus Melayu dengan baik, bagaimana kita akan meyakinkan rakan kita di Sabah dan Sarawak untuk terus yakin dengan kita bagi menerajui pemerintahan Malaysia?" katanya ketika menyampaikan ucapan penangguhan Perhimpunan Agung Umno 2026, di Pusat Dagangan Dunia Kuala Lumpur.
Khaled berkata kelemahan ini akan melunturkan kelayakan dan kelebihan parti Melayu di Semenanjung selaku nakhoda dan pengemudi pembangunan Malaysia.
"Mereka (rakyat Sabah dan Sarawak) sudah pasti berhak bertanya, apakah masih mesti orang Semenanjung yang terus diberikan kelebihan dalam memandu dan memaju Malaysia?
"Apatah lagi kedua-dua wilayah itu kini sangat stabil, sangat bersatu padu dan sedang menunjukkan prestasi yang baik."

Menurut Khaled, mengembalikan penyatuan Melayu bererti mengembalikan keyakinan wilayah Sabah dan Sarawak bahawa Semenanjung berada dalam keadaan baik, saling menyokong dan layak untuk terus menjadi pengemudi pembangunan Malaysia.
"Atas dasar itulah kita mesti menjayakan penyatuan Melayu," katanya.

Isu keyakinan Sabah dan Sarawak menjadi perhatian pada PAU 2026 apabila Timbalan Presiden Mohamad Hasan berkata kedua-dua wilayah itu kini menjadi 'kuasa penentu', dan Umno memerlukan keyakinan mereka untuk membentuk kerajaan.

Sementara itu, Khaled mengumumkan usul menaikkan had umur keahlian Puteri Umno kepada 40 tahun akan diputuskan selepas PRU16, kerana perkara itu perlu dilihat secara menyeluruh termasuk kesannya terhadap Wanita dan parti.
fd3299c3241d6b09: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has proposed that one of the 'SG4' states, particularly Terengganu, hold an election to test prospective political partners' sincerity in pursuing cooperation.
He said this would show whether cooperation in the name of Malay-Muslim unity reflected a genuine willingness to share power or merely benefited one side.

"I would like to propose that after Melaka, we test our friends' sincerity. Let us ask one of the SG4 states to hold an election. Hold it in Terengganu. I want to see what formula you offer," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.
a231eb90bc4a1711: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — The Penang government is unlikely to table a proposed law guaranteeing equal constituency development funds (CDF) at the coming state legislative assembly sitting, due to time constraints.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said he had instructed the state legal adviser to prepare a draft enactment.
“It was presented at the state exco meeting on Wednesday,” he told reporters at a press conference after presenting the Penang2030 eighth-year report card at Holiday Inn Resort today.
He said the state government needed time to examine its details, adding that an engagement session with stakeholders would also be required.
“We have some more time to deliberate on it,” he said.
Chow was responding to DAP’s recent call for Penang to enact legislation ensuring equal development allocations for all state constituencies.
On September 8, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the party’s central executive committee had resolved to ask the Penang government to introduce the law.
“CDF should be given equally, regardless of the political background of the elected representatives,” Loke said then.

He said the legislation would guarantee fair and equal treatment for all Penang assemblymen, irrespective of political affiliation, and that the same principle should be extended to the federal level and adopted by every state government.
The Penang government currently provides each opposition assemblyman with RM60,000 annually, while government assemblymen receive RM500,000 in yearly constituency allocations.
Last August, Chow said the state would await a decision from DAP’s national leadership before moving ahead with such legislation.
He said Penang had provided allocations to opposition representatives for many years, although they had repeatedly sought higher amounts during state assembly sittings.
73e0e8ade974859a: MISANO: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi fired a warning to his MotoGP championship rivals by breaking the all-time lap record at his home track of Misano on Saturday to take pole position for the San Marino Grand Prix ahead of Ducati's Marc Marquez.
Bezzecchi became the first rider to break the one minute and 30 seconds barrier, clocking 1:29.982 to give Aprilia pole on the team's home turf.
"It was a good lap, I'm happy because the qualifying wasn't easy. I met a lot of yellow flags and it was difficult to find the concentration," Bezzecchi said.
"In the first stint I stayed on the track one lap more just to have a lap time and fortunately it was my best one because in the second stint I couldn't have a clean lap."
The Italian complained by raising his hand when LCR Honda's Johann Zarco impeded him and the stewards said they were investigating the incident.
Bezzecchi will be joined by Marquez and Gresini Racing's Fermin Aldeguer on the front row.
Marquez attempted to better his time twice late in the session but pulled out of both flying laps as he tried to ride over the limits on the turns.
"Last year my pace was a bit better, but this year it looks like Marco is super fast, extremely fast in the fast corners," Marquez said.

"Let's see if we can fight, but the target was the front row. When I stopped in the box, I saw the 1:29 (from Bezzecchi). I said, 'OK, ciao pole position, I will not arrive there because I knew where was my limits.'
"I override, I tried to push my 100%. It was enough to achieve the target, not enough to be in pole position."
VR46 Racing's Fabio Di Giannantonio went fourth fastest while championship leader Jorge Martin was only fifth fastest and has Honda's Luca Marini alongside him on the second row.
Martin leads the championship with 256 points while Marquez is second (237 points) and Bezzecchi third (232 points).
KTM's Pedro Acosta, VR46 Racing's Franco Morbidelli and Gresini Racing's Alex Marquez - who crashed twice in the qualifying session - will start on the third row.
Francesco Bagnaia, who held the previous lap record at Misano, continued to struggle aboard his Ducati - as he has all season - and will start 14th on the grid after failing to advance from Q1 to Q2.
54ca52a3237d1b8b: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 12 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow has ordered all state executive councillors to identify Penang2030 initiatives under their portfolios that have not been started or completed.
He said the directive was issued several weeks ago, and that he was personally monitoring the outstanding initiatives.
“I have given an order a few weeks ago for every exco to list down things that they have not completed, and I hope that they will take action to complete it.
“I want to hand over Penang nicely to the successor,” he told reporters after presenting the Penang2030 eighth-year report card at the Holiday Inn Resort here today.
Chow said he would seek explanations from state excos overseeing portfolios that had recorded slow progress.
Asked to rate his administration’s performance this term, he gave his standard reply of 70 per cent.

About eight in 10 key Penang2030 targets had either been achieved or were progressing, he said, covering areas including welfare and housing assistance, local government reform, tourism, education, agriculture, entrepreneurship and youth development.
He identified agriculture as one area requiring further improvement.
“Penang has established 384 urban farms, but agricultural productivity remains below the state’s target,” he said during his presentation.
The initial target had been to establish 100 urban farms; once that was achieved, the target was raised to 500, he said.

The state intends to expand technology-assisted methods such as smart agriculture, precision farming and vertical farming, drawing on Penang’s electrical and electronics industry and engineering talent.
Reducing household water consumption was another target the state has struggled to hit.
“If we can cut at least 28 litres, or ideally 55 litres to 220 litres per person per day, that is considered a win for us already,” he said.
He said the national average currently stands at 225 litres per capita daily, against the World Health Organisation’s recommended 165 litres.
“There is still much to be done. There is always much to be done because a government’s job is never done,” Chow said.
“Today is not a celebration. Today is for us to look back so we can orientate ourselves forward more precisely.”

He said several major infrastructure projects would continue beyond 2030, adding that he would leave it to his successor to decide whether existing programmes should be maintained or replaced with new priorities.
955531ab7f99812e: KUALA LUMPUR: The days of a single party forming the government on its own are over, said Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the party must recognise this reality, which was the basis for president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's proposal to form political understandings with other parties.
"The era of one party forming the government, in my view, is over.
"Let us not dream that one party can form the government, that Umno can form the government on its own," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
a057ffd8d90706a2: SEPT 12 — The rise of the far right in Germany and Sweden cannot simply be explained as a sudden outbreak of xenophobia.
Nor should it be reduced to Vladimir Putin, the war in Ukraine or some mysterious resurgence of European nationalism.
Its roots are deeper.

They lie partly in a growing perception among sections of European society that the political centre has ceased to listen to their anxieties about migration, welfare, identity, security and the pace of social change.
Malaysia should pay attention.
The political circumstances are obviously different.
However, the underlying mechanism — the gradual migration of mainstream politics towards harder positions when voters believe established parties are ignoring them — is increasingly familiar.
Germany provides the clearest warning.
The Alternative for Germany (AfD), once confined largely to the political margins, has just emerged victorious in the Saxony-Anhalt state election.
It secured 39 of the state parliament's 83 seats, although other parties continue to resist forming a government with it. It captured 44 percent of the votes.
Nationally, its strength has also made the traditional German political firewall increasingly difficult to maintain. Russian interferance alone cannot explain this.
For decades during the Cold War, West Germany lived beside something considerably more formidable than today's Russian Federation: the Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact.
Soviet military power was positioned directly across the divided German frontier.
Germany survived this proximity without becoming politically unrecognisable.
What has changed is the domestic political psychology.

The refugee crisis of Germany began in 2015, followed by subsequent migration and then the enormous displacement generated by the Ukraine war, altered public perceptions of borders, citizenship and the responsibilities of the welfare state.
This does not mean that refugees simply enter Europe and automatically receive unlimited welfare benefits.
European asylum and social-security systems are considerably more complicated than that.
Ukrainian refugees in Germany, for example, can qualify for social assistance when they meet residence and financial-need requirements.
Either way, AfD does not want the Ukrainians in Germany.
But politics is driven as much by perceptions of fairness as by the precise wording of statutes.
Europe's Schengen system compounds this political sensitivity because it represents one of the most ambitious experiments in human mobility ever attempted.
Today 29 countries participate fully in the Schengen Area, encompassing more than 450 million people, with internal border controls generally abolished.
Schengen is an extraordinary achievement.
But every achievement produces political obligations.

If citizens believe the external borders are inadequately controlled, or that governments cannot distinguish efficiently between refugees, economic migrants, irregular migrants and people whose asylum applications have been rejected.
Freedom of movement can gradually be interpreted as loss of control.
That perception has political consequences.
Sweden demonstrates them vividly now.
For generations, Sweden was associated with social democracy, an extensive welfare state, humanitarian internationalism and relatively liberal approaches towards asylum.
Yet immigration, integration and crime have progressively transformed Swedish politics.

The author argues that Malaysia should learn from the European Union, particularly Germany and Sweden, by addressing legitimate public concerns without allowing mainstream politics to drift towards more extreme identity-based positions. — AFP pic
The Sweden Democrats have moved from political isolation into becoming indispensable to the country's governing right-wing bloc.
Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson has even indicated his willingness to include them formally in government should his bloc prevail in the September 13 election.
Meanwhile, Sweden has dramatically tightened migration policy.
Asylum applications have fallen to a 40-year low, while the government has introduced measures including tougher residency and citizenship rules.
It is even offering substantial financial assistance to some immigrants who voluntarily return to their countries of origin.
Something profound has therefore happened.
Policies that might once have been dismissed as belonging to the radical right have gradually migrated towards the political mainstream.
This is the real lesson for Malaysia.
Malaysia is not Germany or Sweden. Its historical formation, constitutional structure, ethnic composition and political economy are completely different.
Malaysia has also managed pluralism for decades through institutions and political arrangements peculiar to its own history.
Yet Malaysia is experiencing its own rightward gravitational pull.
Here the principal fault line is not Middle Eastern or North African immigration.
It is the increasingly intense competition overMalay-Muslim political identity.
When mainstream parties fear losing their core constituencies, they begin borrowing the vocabulary, symbols and political priorities of parties further to their right. This creates a dangerous cycle.
A party adopts harder positions to prevent its supporters from defecting.
Its competitors then move further right to distinguish themselves.
Before long, the entire political spectrum has shifted even though the electorate itself may not have moved by the same distance.
Germany demonstrates precisely how this can happen.
The AfD does not need to govern Germany nationally to influence Germany.

Its political importance already lies in forcing other parties to discuss immigration, borders, asylum, national identity, Ukraine and relations with Russia in terms substantially different from those of a decade ago.
Sweden offers an even stronger illustration. The Sweden Democrats spent years outside the political establishment.
Yet policies associated with their critique of immigration have increasingly shaped government policy.
The radical flank can therefore win without capturing the state.
It wins when everybody else begins speaking its political language.
Malaysia must avoid this trap.
Malay's concerns about economic security, social mobility, education, cultural confidence and political representation cannot simply be dismissed.
Neither should the concerns of Chinese, Indians, Sabahans, Sarawakians or other communities about equal citizenship and institutional fairness.
Suppressing legitimate anxieties merely creates political space for more extreme actors to monopolise them.
But acknowledging anxieties is different from weaponising them.
The European experience demonstrates what happens when complicated questions of migration, inequality, welfare, crime and national identity are compressed into a single politics of resentment.
Once every problem acquires an ethnic, religious or civilisational explanation, democratic politics becomes increasingly zero-sum.
Malaysia is already susceptible to such tendencies.
If every election becomes a referendum on which ethnic or religious community is supposedly gaining at the expense of another, the political centre will steadily hollow out.
The lesson from Germany and Sweden is therefore not that Malaysia should fear a European-style far right.
It is that Malaysia should understand how a rightward political tilt actually occurs.
It rarely arrives overnight.

It develops incrementally when citizens lose confidence in institutions, when mainstream parties become afraid of explaining complicated realities, and when political entrepreneurs discover that identity is easier to mobilise than policy.
Europe's predicament should consequently be studied rather than mocked.
Germany and Sweden show that prosperous, educated and institutionally strong democracies are not immune from political polarisation. Economic development alone does not guarantee moderation.

Malaysia's task is to prevent legitimate Malay-Muslim concerns from being transformed into permanent civilisational insecurity while simultaneously ensuring that non-Malay Malaysians never feel that their citizenship is conditional.
That requires something more difficult than moving left or right.
It requires restoring confidence in the political centre.
For when the centre stops explaining, listening and governing effectively, the political extremes do not have to conquer it. They merely wait for the centre to move towards them.
This is a major problem confronting Malaysia. Learning from Germany and Sweden provides an evidence-based discourse to prevent the lurch to the right.
84479b3bea6ede17: KUALA LUMPUR: It is up to under-performing Lee Zii Jia to decide whether he wants to resume training with the national players at the Academy Badminton Malaysia (ABM) in Bukit Kiara, with the BA of Malaysia (BAM) making it clear there are no plans for a special meeting with the independent shuttler.

BAM president Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the association had yet to receive any feedback from Zii Jia's camp on the possibility of using ABM's facilities as the former All England champion looks to arrest his alarming decline.
The association's performance committee chairman Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei has welcomed Zii Jia to rejoin the national squad's training on several occasions.
It is understood that the world No. 58 have not attended training at ABM since June because of his competition schedule, while BAM is also unaware of his plans.

"I had discussed it with Chong Wei but he is now in the United States, so he was not here today. But, at the end of the day, it is up to Zii Jia," said Tengku Zafrul after chairing the BAM council meeting at ABM here today.
"For us, we want to focus on the singles players we have now, as well as the juniors and the pipeline."
Asked whether BAM would take the initiative to contact Zii Jia and meet him to discuss training arrangements, Tengku Zafrul said there were no such plans.
"We don't have any plan to meet with Zii Jia," Tengku Zafrul added.
He explained that the council had already decided to open ABM's training sessions to all professional players for the benefit of the country, without requiring them to rejoin BAM.
"Training together is something we have already decided on at the council before. It is not just for Zii Jia, but is open to all independent players. They are welcome and can join at any time.
"Actually, during the Thomas Cup, he was quite cooperative. He came for training twice a week," he said.
Tengku Zafrul also stressed that BAM could not force any independent player to train with the national squad, as it respected their separate goals and training plans.
Zii Jia's latest setback was a shock second-round defeat by unheralded Taiwan world No. 88 Wu Zhe Ying at the ongoing Vietnam Open.
Former international Ong Ewe Hock described the former All England champion as "a ship floating aimlessly in the sea without a captain" following the defeat.
Currently, world No. 6 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani are the only independent players who train twice a week with the BAM squad.
cf613c7330948f50: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan has reiterated his call for the party to build its own strength, warning that other parties want to see its downfall.
He said Umno could not rely on others to help it regain its strength and must learn from past disappointments.
"Do not dream in broad daylight, because not a single party wants to see us rise again. They all want to see us buried," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Without naming any party, he said many had sought to bring about Umno's downfall, only to end up in disarray themselves.
"But those who wanted to do so, Datuk Seri President, ended up reading their own last rites. Look at them now, in disarray and fighting among themselves."
Mohamad said a strong Umno would be better equipped to face challenges and prevent others from exploiting its perceived weakness.
"We have experienced what it is like to be let down. So, let us not be disappointed repeatedly.
"Although the president has spoken of political understanding, let it remain an understanding. Do not get so carried away that we forget our priority is to build our own strength."
He urged delegates to prepare their election machinery and called on Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to keep the party united and negotiate carefully ahead of the state election.
"Negotiate properly. If it is not right, do not proceed. We have dignity. Do not sacrifice our dignity to gain power.
"Umno has never depended on the goodwill of others. It was not founded through the goodwill of others. It was founded because we wanted to defend the Malays, our race and our religion," he added.
Melaka is edging closer to a state election after Rauf hinted yesterday that the state assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month.
ccafdff50faa73e9: KUALA LUMPUR: The Defence Ministry is stepping up efforts to counter growing cognitive warfare threats, including disinformation, digital propaganda and the use of artificial intelligence to influence how Malaysians think and act.

Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said such threats were no longer confined to conventional warfare but had evolved into hybrid forms that could exploit technology and social divisions.
"Cognitive warfare is a planned strategy to influence the way people think, assess information, make decisions and act.

"All this is done systematically through disinformation and hoaxes, digital propaganda, exploitation of algorithms and psychological operations," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
The Umno vice-president said there were already efforts to systematically use artificial intelligence and other advanced technologies to influence public opinion and behaviour.
The objective, he said, was to create social instability, deepen polarisation and trigger divisions and disharmony within society.
Khaled said such threats were particularly concerning because they could also be used to erode national identity and fuel religious and racial tensions.
"The Defence Ministry is very concerned about this and is doing its best to develop an integrated strategy to face this extraordinary threat," he said.
He said the ministry's focus included strengthening what he called "people's resilience" so Malaysians would be less vulnerable to manipulation and attempts to divide society.
Khaled said a resilient population was an important element of credible deterrence and could serve as a strong line of defence when the country faced security threats.
He cited Iran and Ukraine as examples of countries where people had remained resilient and difficult to divide despite coming under attack.
Khaled said Umno, as a political party, also had a role to play in strengthening national resilience by promoting mature, rational and non-extreme politics.
"We must practise mature politics. Politics that is rational, not emotional and not extreme," he said.
He said every Umno leader was also a community leader and therefore had a responsibility to prevent members of society from becoming easily influenced by divisive propaganda.
"People's resilience is ultimately about our ability to remain united and not be extreme or easily influenced by propaganda that divides us.
"Most importantly, it is about patriotism and our willingness to help the country when needed," he said.
Khaled said Umno would support the Armed Forces in efforts to strengthen national resilience and ensure the country was prepared to face threats in whatever form they might take.
He said controlling political instability and strengthening public resilience were also important to Malaysia's broader national security.
"Umno will not allow this cognitive threat to undermine the identity, thinking and actions of the Malay community and Malaysian society," he said.

075b56c745bf4e95: NEW DELHI: Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian said on Saturday that the Middle East does not need the United States to be a "regional policeman", with the two countries at war and vying for control of the Strait of Hormuz.
"We do not need a regional policeman," he said on the sidelines of a BRICS summit in India during a meeting with Malaysian prime minister Anwar Ibrahim.
"The territorial integrity and security of the region can only be guaranteed by its main players and the countries that comprise it," he added, according to the Iranian presidency.
Iran has been at war since Feb 28, when US-Israeli strikes killed its supreme leader.
The Islamic republic retaliated with attacks across the region and blockaded the Strait of Hormuz, through which one-fifth of the world's oil previously flowed.
Iran and the US have since been vying for control of the strategic waterway.
The strait was free to transit before the war, but Iran now requires vessels to obtain permission and is considering a mechanism to impose service fees.
Ships that do not comply are regularly targeted by Iranian strikes, while the US periodically bombs the Iranian coastline to challenge the Islamic republic's control of the strait.
More than six months into the Middle East war, the blockade continues to drive up oil prices, which soared past $100 a barrel this week.
"Despite all the injustices suffered by our people, we neither desire war nor its continuation. Peace remains our priority," Pezeshkian added.
d04fdbb902fafa29: KUALA LUMPUR: Malays should learn from the way the Chinese community works together politically despite belonging to different parties, said Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
Khaled said Chinese political groups might disagree and engage in fierce political debate, but remained united when issues affecting the community's long-term interests arose.
"There is one important characteristic that needs our attention.
"They may be in different political parties, but they never focus on their differences," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Khaled said this approach had enabled different Chinese political groups to maintain a common position on issues they regarded as important to the community.
"They may argue with one another, but they do not truly split," he said.

He cited issues including Chinese schools, recognition of the Unified Examination Certificate (UEC) and the interests of Kampung Baru as examples of areas where Chinese groups continued to speak collectively.
"When there is an issue involving the future and interests of the Chinese community, some will shout and some will speak quietly. But they will not stop speaking together.
Khaled said Malays should adopt a similar approach by working together on issues affecting the community even when they belonged to different political parties.
He said Malay political fragmentation had weakened the community's political position and made it harder to advance shared interests.
He said Malay unity should not require everyone to abandon their respective political identities, but should allow them to come together when common interests were at stake.
Khaled said mechanisms such as Rumah Bangsa, Musyawarah Nasional and Tafahum Siyasi could provide platforms for such cooperation.
He said the objective was to build a stronger and more cohesive Malay political voice while respecting differences in ideology and political affiliation.
d0f7ac6feff95bd5: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 12 — Discussions are under way with all relevant parties on the drafting of a new law to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir.

He said several meetings had been held with representatives of the academic community and university administrators, while discussions with other groups, including students, would continue over the coming days.

“I have already met with Student Representative Councils and asked the National Student Representative Council, which represents students from all universities, to organise their own groups, whether Group A or Group B, representing those who agree and disagree, so that we can bring the views together and consider them.

“This is because I want the new law to be comprehensive,” he told reporters while visiting the Media Lounge in conjunction with the 2026 Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur here today.
He said the new law should not only take into account current needs, but also address the challenges the country may face in the future.

Zambry said this is important as the UUCA, introduced in 1971, covers various aspects of higher education institutions, including the establishment and administration of universities, as well as matters concerning students.
Against this backdrop, he said, changes in the higher education landscape and the current legal framework need to be taken into account when drafting the new law.
“I have said repeatedly that UUCA was introduced 54 years ago. There have obviously been changes, and some may say that it is no longer suitable,” he said.
In August, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would repeal UUCA in its entirety, with a Bill on the matter to be tabled in Parliament this year.

Anwar said the proposal to repeal the Act aimed to give student movements in the country greater freedom and democratic space, after taking into account memoranda and views from student leaders, who wanted comprehensive changes to the Act. — Bernama

8124e2b535775a6b: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno will decide on a proposal to raise the age limit for Puteri Umno membership only after the 16th General Election (GE16), said party vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.

Khaled, who chairs the party's Constitution and Rules Committee, said the proposal required careful consideration as any change would affect not only Puteri Umno but also Wanita Umno and the party as a whole.
He said the proposal had received strong support from Puteri Umno, but the party needed to assess its wider implications before making a decision.
"This is an issue that is not easy to decide.

"The proposal must be looked at as a whole because it does not only bring changes to Puteri, but will also have an impact on Wanita and, of course, the party as a whole," he said in his winding-up speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
Khaled said the committee had therefore decided to defer a decision on the proposal until after GE16.
He said this would allow the party and its wings to focus fully on preparations for the next general election.
"For that reason, the party has decided to make a decision on the proposal after the next general election.
"This is because we want to ensure that everyone gives their full attention and focus to the effort to win the election," he said.
It was reported that Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi had proposed raising the wing's membership age limit to 40 from the current 35.
The proposal was among several motions received by the Constitution and Rules Committee this year.
Khaled said the party appreciated Puteri Umno's efforts to strengthen the wing and recognised its importance to Umno's future.
a3111078cb0cda56: PETALING JAYA: Police have frozen the bank accounts and financial assets of a second pilot detained over a drug smuggling syndicate linked to the arrest of a Malaysia Airlines pilot in Jakarta in July.

Narcotics crime investigation department director Hussein Omar Khan said the pilot, suspected of acting as a middleman between the Malaysia Airlines pilot and a drug syndicate, will be held for 60 days under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
Hussein said investigators are examining the pilot's bank accounts and other financial records, though he did not disclose the amount of money found in the accounts.

"He (the second pilot) is part of a syndicate involved in the flow of money from drug sales. He played a role in helping the (first) pilot receive and transfer the money," Berita Harian quoted him as saying.
The pilot, in his 30s, was arrested in the Klang Valley on Sept 7, bringing the number of people arrested in Malaysia in connection with the case to seven.
The first Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta on July 29 after being found in possession of 25kg of ecstasy pills and 2.7g of methamphetamine.
On Sept 4, police said they arrested six other Malaysian men following questioning of the 39-year-old pilot by a team of Bukit Aman officers from Aug 11 to 15.
41f2917a8dcceff9: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah tourism players have urged the government to introduce targeted package tour subsidies to help offset airfares between Kuala Lumpur and Kota Kinabalu ahead of Visit Sabah Year 2027.
They said the targeted approach would cushion packaged tour costs without broadly subsidising airfares, ensuring support reaches operators driving arrivals into the state.

They urged authorities to intensify enforcement against illegal van operations.
They called for a review of subsidised diesel leakage for unauthorised commercial use and support for licensed operators to ensure safe, insured and regulated transport remains viable.
The illegal van operators can undercut the tourism industry by using Budi diesel meant for other purposes, including the reported use of the 400-litre Budi diesel allocation.
They urged licensing and local authorities to regulate unlicensed short-term rental accommodation mushrooming across Sabah to ensure visitor safety and confidence.
a287f259d4bfdf4c: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended an invitation to Ethiopia to establish an Embassy in Kuala Lumpur during his bilateral meeting with his counterpart, Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
Malaysia’s reopening of its embassy in Addis Ababa in September 2025, after 43 years, marked significant progress in bilateral relations.

The discussion also touched on the positive momentum generated by reciprocal visits by both leaders. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed visited Malaysia in 2024, while Anwar visited Ethiopia in 2025.
The Prime Minister said it has been agreed that the first Bilateral Consultation will take place in Kuala Lumpur next year to further strengthen cooperation between the two countries.
Other areas of cooperation discussed included halal products, agriculture, food security, pharmaceuticals, digital services, renewable energy and tourism.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation for Ethiopia’s support for Malaysia’s engagement with Brics during the bilateral meeting that took place on the sidelines of the 18th Brics Leaders’ Summit here.
Malaysia’s participation in the Summit is in its capacity as a Brics Partner Country, a status it has held since Jan 1, 2025.
Ethiopia, the world’s most populous landlocked country, ranked as Malaysia’s 26th-largest trading partner in the African continent in 2023.

Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Ethiopia stood at RM446.8 million in 2023, with Malaysia’s exports to Ethiopia valued at RM358.6 million, representing a 24.6 per cent increase from the previous year. — Bernama

* Editor’s note: Brics is a bloc of major emerging economies that originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, but has since expanded to include countries such as Ethiopia, Egypt, Iran and the UAE.
e773edc74a6eb88b: CLEON: Investigators suspect that a train derailment in northwest France which injured 44, one gravely, was the result of sabotage, a police source told AFP on Saturday.
A fragment of rail was found on the track, with the possibility of a malicious act being treated as the main line of inquiry as a result, the source said.
Carrying 186 passengers, the train was running between the Normandy cities of Rouen and Caen when it derailed around 7.45pm (1745 GMT) Friday close to Renault's factory in the town of Cleon.
Authorities activated a mass-casualty response plan, with 130 firefighters, five medical teams and 80 vehicles drafted in.
An AFP photographer saw a mass of railway staff working around the train on Saturday morning.

Rouen prosecutor Sebastien Gallois said 44 people were injured including an 18-year-old woman evacuated "in a critical condition", while tests for drugs and alcohol on the train driver had come back negative.
"Suddenly there were a few jolts, and then after about three seconds it got stronger and stronger," one of the passengers, Louis, 24, told ICI Normandie radio.
"I couldn't stay in my seat any more," he said. "The windows partially shattered, the stones from the track came into the carriage. It was really shocking. I'm still shaking."
Those who escaped unharmed were taken to a room made available by Cleon's mayor, according to the authorities.
SNCF Reseau, which controls the French rail network, told AFP that traffic on the line had been suspended and power to the tracks cut to allow emergency services to operate.
According to SNCF, the accident caused "major disruptions" to rail traffic between Rouen and Caen and between Caen and Le Havre in both directions.
A spokesperson for SNCF Reseau said on Saturday morning that services had resumed.
On the Rouen-Caen line, which usually sees 10 return services per day and six at weekends, a replacement bus service has been set up, SNCF Voyageurs said.
According to the spokesperson, the train will only be lifted off the line once the public prosecutor allows it, with investigations into the cause of the derailment still ongoing.
SNCF insisted that it would offer "full cooperation in complete transparency" to the inquiry.
d36c3d0fc567724b: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi have discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in strategic sectors, particularly the semiconductor industry.

Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said Malaysia and India possess complementary strengths that could be harnessed through industrial cooperation, supply chain integration, talent development, and bilateral investment.

"I also raised the need to facilitate and expedite the entry of Malaysian exports into the Indian market, creating greater opportunities for Malaysian companies to tap into India's large and rapidly growing market," Anwar said in a Facebook post today.
"God willing, Malaysia and India will continue to strengthen this mutually beneficial friendship for the prosperity of the peoples of both countries," he added.
Anwar met Modi at Hyderabad House in New Delhi after arriving in India with the Malaysian delegation last night.
He expressed appreciation for the special hospitality extended to the delegation since its arrival in the Indian capital.
Anwar is in India to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit.

During his visit, he is also scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakhstan President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
The summit, themed "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability", will focus on strengthening economic cooperation and advancing trade and investment reforms.
38c8710852b5a738: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah's long-standing undocumented migrant problem continues because of a lack of political will to implement proposed solutions, says former chief justice Tun Richard Malanjum.

He said numerous proposals had been put forward over the years - from recalling wrongfully issued identity cards to introducing a distinct Sabah identity card, a kad warga asing and a pas sementara Sabah - only to be abandoned.
"What has been missing is not a legal mechanism, it is the will to sit down and build one," he said.
Malanjum, a Sabahan, was speaking at the launch of a book, "Citizenship in Crisis: The Ripple Effect of the Undocumented Migrants in Sabah".

The book, authored by Sessions Court judge Dr Melissa Chia, is based on court cases, notes of proceedings from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), archival material from the Sabah Archives and Sabah government, and field interviews.

Malanjum said many foreigners caught up in "Project IC" — which refers to long-standing claims over the illegal issuance of Malaysian identity cards to immigrants in Sabah — were never actually made citizens.

"They stayed and raised families, and now stand before our National Registration Department and our courts, unable to prove who they are," he said, adding that this had created a permanent underclass of stateless children.
He said although the RCI recommended establishing a permanent secretariat to investigate, manage and resolve the problem, it never functioned as intended due to a lack of political will.
Malanjum said the issue was unjust to Sabah, as the entire human, fiscal and social burden was placed on a single state.
He proposed that if the Federation were to regularise any part of this population, it should bear the burden itself.

"Those found eligible for a lawful status should not automatically be concentrated in Sabah, but distributed across the states of Malaysia in proportion to capacity, with the funding to match," he said.
He said freedom of movement under Article 9 of the Federal Constitution cuts both ways, while Sabah retains immigration autonomy under Part VII of the Immigration Act.
Chia recorded two proposals in her book, including a truth and reconciliation commission based on the South African model and an independent tribunal to determine status case by case.
80564de744a7dcc9: PETALING JAYA: Majlis Tertinggi Perikatan Nasional (PN) akan bermesyuarat hujung minggu depan antara lainnya akan membincangkan perlantikan dan penyusunan kepimpinan negeri, kata Ketua Penerangan PN Annuar Musa.

ff15714944254bb5: BERLIN: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said he would be willing to meet Russian president Vladimir Putin at a G20 summit in December, in an interview released Saturday, as efforts intensify to end the conflict.

Washington is seeking to kick-start long-stalled negotiations to find a solution to the conflict, Europe's deadliest since World War II, with US negotiators recently visiting Kyiv and Moscow and president Donald Trump and Putin this week holding talks on the conflict over the phone.

The United States holds this year's presidency of the Group of 20 major economies, which comprises 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union, and culminates in a leaders' summit in Miami in December.

Russia's finance minister has already attended one G20 meeting, causing discomfort among some of Ukraine's allies, and a Russian diplomat said Saturday that Moscow will also send some officials to a G20 energy meeting in Houston next week.
Asked whether he would be willing to meet Putin at the December summit if both leaders were invited, Zelensky told German broadcaster Deutsche Welle: "Yes, of course.
"We have to come. We have to meet, to speak, and make decisions.
"It's not about words. What I will tell him or what he wants to tell me, it doesn't matter. It doesn't matter. Matters only result. Result matters. That's it."

Last weekend, US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow and Putin and Trump also discussed the war earlier in the week in what the Kremlin termed an "extremely frank" and constructive hour-long phone call.
Diplomatic efforts intensify

In the Deutsche Welle interview, which took place Friday in Canada, Zelensky said that Witkoff and Kushner's visit was a "good signal", and it was important the pair had visited Kyiv as well as Moscow.
"It's respect to our people," he said.
Zelensky has also announced he plans to meet Trump in late September, as Washington pushes for fresh face-to-face talks between Moscow and Kyiv.
Asked about Ukraine's position ahead of possible negotiations, Zelensky responded: "Ukraine now is much more stronger than last year on the battlefield."
Russia was sustaining heavy battlefield losses, paying a "big price" for "very slow moves on the battlefield". he said.
"That's why we think that we have now good position for negotiations."
Kyiv has said the talks could happen as early as this month, but the Kremlin on Monday said it was "too early" to discuss a venue or dates.
Several previous rounds of negotiations have failed. Trust between the sides is low, and there is no sign that Moscow or Kyiv have shifted their positions.
Both Moscow and Kyiv have escalated long-range strikes on each other in recent months, leading to the highest civilian death toll since the early days of the war.
Zelensky also repeated his call for Ukraine's allies to provide more interceptor missiles to fend off Russian air attacks.
"Russia produces... today 140 ballistic missiles per month. So, according to the rules of Nato, if you want to destroy 140, you need 280... You will never have 280 missiles per month," he said.
It was a "huge challenge" to have 100 a month, he said.
307fb5109c41d26d: KAJANG: Polis sedang mengesan dua lelaki yang meloloskan diri dengan sebuah kereta selepas cuba diperiksa anggota Unit Kereta Peronda (MPV) di Jalan Semenyih berhampiran lampu isyarat Kajang Prima, petang semalam.

27c2076b0ecfe4d0: SEPT 12 — Every semester, academics face an increasingly familiar reality: students are using artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT and Gemini as part of their academic work.

AI is no longer something universities can simply keep outside the classroom; it is embedded in the digital environment where undergraduate assignments, postgraduate research and everyday learning now take place.
Yet much of the institutional response has focused on control — oral defences, offline in-class writing, restrictions on AI use and controversial AI-detection tools.
While these measures have a place, relying on them as our primary defence risks missing a much bigger question: what exactly are we trying to assess?
A persistent flaw in our current thinking is the assumption that students can somehow be separated from technology.
The generation entering our lecture halls has grown up with smartphones and instant access to information.
Technology is not an occasional addition to their learning environment; it is part of it.

Returning entirely to analogue forms of assessment may solve one problem while creating another, especially as students enter workplaces where the ability to work critically and responsibly with AI is increasingly valuable.
The real challenge is not that students are using software to assist with academic tasks.

It is that many assessment models still place enormous weight on the final product — the polished report, essay or written answer — while revealing relatively little about the human process behind it.
If an assignment can be completed convincingly with a single AI prompt, perhaps we should also question what that assignment was designed to measure.
Protecting academic integrity requires more than catching students using AI; it requires us to reconsider what evidence of learning should look like.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The author argues that universities should redesign assessments to evaluate students’ critical thinking and intellectual contribution when using AI, rather than focusing mainly on detecting or restricting its use. — Unsplash pic
This responsibility does not belong to students or lecturers alone; it must be shared across the entire higher education ecosystem.
In practice, rather than asking students to submit every conversation they have had with an AI tool, assessments could require a concise AI-use log or selected prompt trail.
Students could identify key prompts used, highlight suggestions they accepted or rejected, point out factual errors and explain how they verified information using credible sources.
The purpose is to make the student’s intellectual contribution visible: what they questioned, changed, verified and ultimately decided.
Assessment could also require students to interrogate AI-generated answers rather than simply reproduce them.
They might compare different AI responses, test an AI-generated argument against academic literature or explain why a seemingly convincing answer is actually weak.
This shifts the student’s role from passive recipient to critical evaluator.
Furthermore, universities could rethink the dominance of the one-off final submission.

Instead of receiving only a polished essay at the end of the semester, lecturers could assess selected stages of the student’s intellectual journey, from the initial idea and AI-assisted exploration to verification and final revision.
None of this means academic misconduct should become acceptable because AI exists.
Passing off AI-generated work as one’s own or fabricating references remain serious integrity concerns.
But academic integrity should not become weaker in the age of AI.
It should become more demanding.
Students should be expected not merely to produce an answer, but to demonstrate judgment, verification, intellectual ownership and the ability to defend the choices behind it.
The goal of modern higher education must extend beyond training students to produce polished documents.
AI can generate remarkably fluent text in seconds.
But students cannot outsource the responsibility to judge whether that text is accurate, credible, ethical and worth accepting.
Perhaps the question we should ask is no longer simply, “Did the student use AI?”
A more meaningful question is, “What intellectual work did the student still have to do?”
If universities can redesign assessment around that question, AI will not signal the end of academic integrity.
It may instead force us to define it more clearly than we ever have before.

6230f2455034ed10: KUALA LUMPUR: The BA of Malaysia (BAM) is seriously considering an attractive monetary incentive for shuttlers to end a 20-year wait for an Asian Games gold medal in Aichi-Nagoya.

Realising there is no special incentive programme for Asian Games medallists apart from the rewards offered by the National Sports Council (NSC), BAM president Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz said the association would consider rewarding gold medallists as an added boost for the Games, which will be held from Sept 19-Oct 4.

The NSC's national incentive scheme (Shakam) offers RM80,000 for a gold medal, while BAM will look into introducing its own incentive in a bid to end Malaysia's wait since men's doubles pair Koo Kien Keat-Tan Boon Heong struck gold in Doha in 2006.

"I didn't realise it was that long. The last time was in 2006 in Doha, when we won gold. Of course, the NSC will provide a prize, but BAM will also look at what we can afford at that time," said Tengku Zafrul after the BAM council meeting at the Academy Badminton Malaysia here today.
"We will also talk to our sponsors, as they usually provide incentives as well. We can discuss it with them, and then BAM will look at what we can afford, especially for a gold medal.
"I think it's a good idea, and we will consider it."
Tengku Zafrul said the association has specific internal targets for its Asian Games squad, although the official target is one silver and one bronze.

"I will meet the players who will be going to the Asian Games on Monday, and I hope they will stay focused and do their best to deliver for the country, We will not be announcing our internal targets," added Tengku Zafrul.
"We just don't want to put pressure on the players by announcing them. We want them to go all out and give their best."

Malaysia's best bets for gold are independent world No. 6 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani and scratch pair Aaron Chia-Tee Kai Wun, who have an outside chance in a highly competitive men's doubles battle in Aichi-Nagoya.
Meanwhile, BAM also confirmed several key decisions, including a 100 per cent increase in the total prize money for local tournaments organised by the association.
BAM currently offers around RM200,000 in total prize money for its local tournaments, which will increase to RM400,000 next year.
The National Championships offer the highest total prize money, with the amount increasing to RM200,000 from next year.
BAM will also appoint a director of sports science and medicine.
The role is intended to strengthen the high-performance structure and integrate sports science and medical support into the national programme.
New talent identification (TID) and selection rules were also approved, with players no longer required to pursue both singles and doubles simultaneously once they reach the age of 16.
BAM has also begun early preparations for the 2027 SEA Games, where the best shuttlers will be selected in an effort to help Malaysia become overall champions.
685ca68558b7b3b7: KUALA LUMPUR: Closer political cooperation between Umno and Pas could offer political gains but also risks, analysts said, as Umno prepares to form a committee to explore cooperation with Pas.

Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the proposed understanding would allow Umno to keep its options open while assessing whether closer cooperation with Pas was politically viable, including gauging the reactions of its grassroots, Pas and existing political partners.
"Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has clarified that the 'Grand Collaboration' is not a merger but an understanding aimed at avoiding damaging electoral clashes.

"Therefore, it is a serious opening for negotiations, but its significance will depend on whether both parties can agree on candidates, constituencies and their relationships with other political partners," he said when contacted.
Umno and Pas have traditionally competed for Malay-Muslim voters, making closer cooperation between the two parties politically significant.

Earlier, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party would form a negotiation committee to explore political cooperation with Pas, following calls by leaders and delegates at the 2026 Umno General Assembly for closer ties.
Tawfik said relations between Umno and Pas leaders had warmed, although trust remained cautious and conditional.
He said reciprocal visits to the parties' assemblies and Zahid's "blue meets green" remark indicated a willingness to reopen political communication.
However, the collapse of the earlier Muafakat Nasional arrangement continued to shape perceptions.
"Umno delegates will want proof that Pas can honour a new agreement, while Pas must also consider its existing relationship with Bersatu and Perikatan Nasional.

"Consequently, a comprehensive alliance remains difficult in the immediate term. A limited electoral understanding, particularly an agreement to avoid three-cornered contests in selected constituencies, is more realistic."

Tawfik said such cooperation could allow both parties to assess each other's sincerity before considering a broader arrangement, while consolidating parts of the Malay vote and preventing support from splitting in marginal constituencies.
"This may improve their chances, especially where three-cornered contests previously benefited their opponents," he said.
However, he said votes could not simply be added together, as some moderate Malay and non-Malay voters might view the partnership as increasingly conservative or exclusively Malay-Muslim.
"This could weaken Barisan Nasional's multiracial appeal and place MCA, MIC and other BN partners in an uncomfortable position," he said.
He added that the pact's electoral value would depend on how it was presented.

"If it is presented as stable and inclusive power-sharing, it may broaden support. If it is framed narrowly around ethnic and religious mobilisation, it could secure the core Malay electorate while losing voters in mixed constituencies," he said.
On the prospects of an Umno-Pas victory in Melaka and significant national gains, Tawfik said BN remained well placed in Melaka, having won 21 of 28 state seats in the 2021 election.
"Cooperation with Pas could further consolidate Malay support and reduce three-cornered contests.
"But significant gains nationally would still depend on disciplined seat negotiations, effective vote transfers and the ability to retain moderate, non-Malay, Sabah and Sarawak voters.
"Therefore, an Umno-Pas pact could strengthen both parties, but it does not automatically guarantee control of Putrajaya."

Meanwhile, geostrategist and Nusantara Academy of Strategic Research senior fellow Professor Dr Azmi Hassan said the sentiment among Umno grassroots was that working with Pas was the only way, as they saw it, to safeguard Malay rights, Islam as the religion of the Federation and the monarchy.
He said trust between Umno grassroots and Pakatan Harapan remained very thin, particularly because DAP was part of the coalition.
"The trust is very thin. So I think that's the reason the blue must meet the green in this particular case," he said, referring to potential cooperation between Umno and Pas.
Asked whether such cooperation could alienate non-Malay voters, Azmi said it would depend on how Umno managed the arrangement.
"They have to demonstrate that they are in the driver's seat, that they are in control, not Pas. So I think that perception is very, very important here," he said.

9b2458c1c2583715: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno must prioritise instilling patriotic and moral values among young Malaysians alongside its pursuit of development, a Melaka delegate said.
Alor Gajah Umno division deputy chief Datuk Dr Mustafa Musa said nurturing these values must begin at a young age, with the principles of the Rukun Negara serving as a foundation.

4a0fb9183e48e53e: DUBAI: Yemen's Riyadh-backed government forces said on Saturday they have struck Iran-allied Houthi fighters in the strategic Red Sea city of Mocha.

Following a week-long offensive, the Houthis on Friday captured Yemen's Red Sea coast, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital artery for Saudi Arabian oil exports as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed amid the US-Iran war.

"The armed forces destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed members of the Houthi terrorist militia backed by the Iranian regime," near the port of the city of Mocha, the government news agency Saba reported.

The spokesman for the Yemeni government forces, Majed Abdullah al-Nazili, said they have also struck the Houthis' "vehicles and members" on the Mocha-Dhubab road, 11 kilometres (7 miles) from the city, according to Saba.
Nazili said Friday they had begun shelling areas in Mocha, and called on citizens not to use the Taiz-Mocha and Mocha-Dhubab roads.
The Houthis seized control of Mocha on Thursday, with their attack driving many to flee to Aden, where the internationally recognised government is based.
On Friday, Houthi media said two Saudi strikes hit Mocha's airport, while a local official said the city's seaport was hit by six missiles of unknown origin.
The Houthi offensive, which started last week, has killed more than 500 people, according to sources on both sides.
It has also displaced about 46,000 people, the UN migration agency said on Friday.
It is part of renewed hostilities in Yemen's civil war that began with the group's takeover of the capital Sanaa in 2014.

bd7d8f0a9aa5af97: NEW DELHI, Sept 12 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his Indian counterpart Narendra Modi discussed deepening semiconductor cooperation and translating it into industry partnerships during their bilateral meeting here today.

Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to increasing bilateral trade and investment, enhancing cooperation across various sectors, as well as implementing measures to facilitate and expedite Malaysian exports to India.

India remains Malaysia’s largest trading partner in the South Asian region, with total trade between the two countries reaching RM79.49 billion (US$18.59 billion) in 2025.

55d8dfeb8143bed5: BERLIN, Sept 12 — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he would be willing to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin at a G20 summit in Miami, in an interview released Saturday, as efforts intensify to end the conflict.

Asked by broadcaster Deutsche Welle if he would meet Putin at the gathering in December if both leaders were invited, he responded: “Yes, of course. We have to come. We have to meet, to speak, and make decisions.

Washington has recently sought to kick-start long-stalled efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, now in its fifth year, with US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visiting Moscow and Kyiv last weekend.

Zelensky said in the DW interview, which took place Friday, that Witkoff and Kushner’s visit was a “good signal”, and it was important the pair had visited Kyiv as well as Moscow.
The United States this year holds the presidency of the Group of 20 major economies, which comprises 19 nations plus the EU and the African Union.
In early September Russian Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was welcomed to a G20 meeting in North Carolina, causing discomfort among Ukraine’s European allies.
And a Russian diplomat said Saturday that Moscow will send some officials to a G20 energy meeting in Houston next week. — AFP
32b27fbaa0fc5255: KUALA KANGSAR: The Public Service Commission (SPA) has filled more than 1,000 nursing vacancies in the public service to date, with open interviews being conducted to expedite the recruitment process.

Its chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Jailani Muhamed Yunus said the move was among its immediate efforts to address the need to fill critical posts, particularly nurses, who are in high demand in the healthcare sector.
"To date, we need more than 1,400 (nurses) and we have already filled more than 1,000. So, we still need several hundred more to be filled urgently.

"These efforts are ongoing from time to time because there are also nursing positions that require candidates to undergo training, and this training takes time," he told reporters after launching the SPA Madani Adopted Village Project Handover Ceremony at Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein today.

Also present were Department of Orang Asli Development (JAKOA) Director-General Muhammad Akmal Ila Ahmad, SPA Secretary Datuk Ikhbal Hanam Mukras and Kampung Orang Asli Ulu Chenein village head Din Alang.

Jailani said the open interview and walk-in methods were introduced early this year through several career carnivals organised by SPA nationwide, providing more opportunities for qualified youths to join the public service.

He said candidates with a diploma in nursing could walk in for an interview, while those who had yet to submit an online application could also complete their SPA application at the interview centre before attending the session.

"This is also a breakthrough effort that we have undertaken to expedite the process. If we use the usual process, there may sometimes be delays. Apart from nurses, SPA is also focusing on filling several other critical positions that require urgent recruitment, including Public Health Assistants (PKA).

"The demand for nurses is quite high, particularly as the healthcare industry has become increasingly important in the country. Therefore, the target is usually (recruiting) nurses into the public service, as the possibly better offers in the private sector mean that a large proportion of them join (the private sector) rather than the public service," he said.

Meanwhile, Jailani, who is also chairman of the Judicial and Legal Service Commission (SPKP), said the government did not prevent civil servants from seeking better employment opportunities after completing their contracts but instead, SPA would ensure that succession plans were implemented by continuously recruiting new personnel.
"They have contracts that have been stipulated in their appointments. However, once their contracts expire, they are free.
"We cannot prevent any government officers from seeking better employment opportunities.

"So, there are no restrictions in this regard and we give them the freedom to do so. Nevertheless, we believe the important thing is the succession plan, and we will find ways to recruit new personnel.
"I am confident that if we go to places such as Felda Chenein in Lenggong, we can find youths who want to join the service," he said.
